clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old female presented with calcifications in the periareolar region of the right breast found on screening mammogram. Diagnostic imaging further characterized these as numerous round and punctate calcifications in a regional distribution in the right subareolar breast, predominantly in the skin, with extension into the nipple. A biopsy was performed, and histopathological evaluation revealed multiple small, variably-sized fragments of foreign material, some angulated and refractile, consistent with glass shards on a background of scar. Subsequent patient history revealed a motor vehicle accident several years prior with chest trauma, leading to the conclusion that the foreign material represented glass shards from a shattered windshield.
